subject: ventures/horse-boarding-stall-profit-calculator
professional: an equine extension farm-business specialist who writes horse-boarding enterprise budgets (and a boarding-barn owner running 10-30 stalls); they check first that profit = board income less variable costs (feed, hay, bedding, labour) less fixed costs, that break-even uses contribution margin per horse, that labour hours per horse are realistic against extension budgets (UMD RES-10 cites about 39 h/month per horse, an Ohio State budget about 21), and that depreciation, interest on investment and the mix of full, partial and pasture board are handled

evidence.correctness: Recomputed by hand (not from the author's tests) for the sample (20 stalls, 85%, $550 board, $40 extras, $160 feed, $55 bedding, 20 min/day at $15, $3,000 fixed, 3% unpaid, $2,000 target): horses 17; labour/horse 20x30.4/60x15 = 152.00; income/horse 590x0.97 = 572.30; margin 572.30-160-55-152 = 205.30; profit 17x205.30-3000 = 490.10; break-even 3000/205.30 = 14.613 horses = 73.06%; break-even board (3000/17+367)/0.97-40 = 520.28; target board (5000/17+367)/0.97-40 = 641.56; owner's effective wage (490.10+2584)/172.27 h = 17.85. node probe.mjs printed exactly these. A second barn (12 stalls, 75%, $700, feed 180, bedding 60, 45 min at $18, $2,500 fixed): by hand margin 700-240-410.40 = 49.60, profit 9x49.60-2500 = -2,053.60, break-even 50.40 horses (420%), break-even board (2500/9+650.40)/1-0 = 928.18; tool matches. Contribution-margin break-even matches the standard cost-volume-profit formula (fixed / unit contribution). DAYS = 30.4 vs 365/12 = 30.417 understates labour by 0.05%, negligible. Wrong output: at 50% occupancy (already losing $947) the tool also says 'Break-even is 73% full and you run 50%. A couple of empty stalls turns it into a loss.' (calc.mjs:67 tests occupancy - breakEvenOcc < 10, which is true for any occupancy below break-even). Input '550,50' (decimal comma) silently becomes $55,050 board and $899,195 profit; '0x226' is read as 550.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features, each run: monthly profit (works); break-even occupancy (works; null when margin <= 0, >100% flagged); break-even and target board price (works, round-trip verified); occupancy table 50-100% plus current, sorted (works); summary text and CSV download functions (sweepCsv, summaryText run); 'within ten points' flag (fires, but also wrongly below break-even); optional fields blank default to 0 (works); validation errors (works). Served page https://marisstella.app/horse-boarding-stall-profit-calculator/ returns 200 with canonical marisstella.app; served llms.txt links marisstella.app (source github.io link is rewritten at deploy). README test command works on Node 22.23.4 (21 pass). No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' from the subject dir: 21 pass, 0 fail, 0.14 s. Six mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: DAYS 30.4->30 caught; priceFor '- p.extras' -> '+ p.extras' caught; k = 1 (bad debt ignored) caught; 'within 10 points' threshold 10->20 survived; effective-wage 'profit + labour' -> 'profit' survived; bad-debt finding '>= 5' -> '> 5' survived. 3 of 6 survived: the core profit/price arithmetic is tested by round trips, the findings (the page's advice) are not; no test asserts the below-break-even case.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (90 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs, index.html. Pure functions, tests import the shipped module, no dependencies, escaped innerHTML, guarded localStorage. Defects: the profit formula is written twice (profitAt at calc.mjs:43 and inline at calc.mjs:51); num() strips every comma so locale input is mis-read silently (calc.mjs:10); findings are an if/else cascade with an unguarded sign (calc.mjs:67). Acceptable to a senior JS reviewer otherwise.
evidence.claims: Checked against files: 'nothing uploaded' backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR/beacon/WebSocket, local imports only) - pass. No-warranty and not-advice disclaimer present (index.html footer, tested) - pass. Formula list in 'What it does' matches calc.mjs - pass. 'Not decided' list names zoning, insurance, contracts, tax, depreciation, board mix - pass. 'flags it when you run within ten points of it' (index.html:12,103) - partial: it also fires, with wrong text, when below break-even. README 'you know whether the barn pays you for your labour ... and what to charge' - partial: the effective hourly figure is shown only when profit >= 0, so a barn that pays the owner $8.27/h against a $15 wage (board $450) never shows the $8.27. 'Unverified: no market rate is claimed' (VENTURE.yaml) - pass, no rate is claimed. Usage events local-only, opt-out and DNT honoured (usage.mjs) - pass.
evidence.fitness: Walked a barn owner's job: enter barn, read profit and break-even, decide a new board price. For a single-tier full-board barn the answer is usable and the reverse price is right. A boarding-business specialist hits gaps in the first hour: most barns sell several tiers (VT 2006 survey: pasture $163, stall $398, stall+paddock $379 average), each with different feed/labour, and the tool takes one price and one cost per horse; no depreciation or interest on the barn investment, which every extension enterprise budget carries (user must fold it into 'fixed'); per-horse labour is the only labour, so arena dragging, fence repair and management time go into fixed unexplained; the sample's 20 min/day (10.1 h/month) is half the Ohio State and a quarter of the UMD per-horse labour figure, and at 21 h/month (41.4 min/day) the sample barn loses $2,274.78 instead of making $490.10, so the worked example shows the opposite of the tool's own thesis.
evidence.domain: Compared with extension horse-boarding enterprise budgets (UMD Extension RES-10 'Horse Boarding' and the Ohio State budget it cites, per their stated per-horse labour of about 39 and 21 h/month; PDF could not be downloaded through the proxy, figures from the search result's quotation) and with the VT 2006 boarding survey (sites.ext.vt.edu/newsletter-archive/fmu/2006-12/horseboarding.html, fetched). Method matches the textbook partial budget / CVP: variable cost per horse, fixed cost, contribution margin, break-even. Departures a specialist would mark: no depreciation and interest-on-investment lines (only listed as not decided); no board-type mix; bad debt modelled as a share of billed board but horses still fed, which is correct; labour default far below extension figures. Sound arithmetic, junior-level enterprise budget.

defects.what: The 'within ten points of break-even' warning fires for every occupancy below break-even, telling an owner already losing $947 a month at 50% (break-even 73%) that 'a couple of empty stalls turns it into a loss'. The condition needs 0 <= occupancy - breakEvenOcc.

The owner's effective hourly pay, the README's headline answer, is shown only when profit >= 0; a barn that loses money at the chosen wage but still pays the owner something (board $450: $8.27/h against $15) never shows it.
Findings logic is untested: threshold 10->20, effective wage profit+labour->profit and bad-debt >=5 -> >5 all left 21 tests green (3 of 6 mutants survived); no test covers occupancy below break-even.
num() strips every comma and accepts any Number() syntax: '550,50' becomes $55,050 board (profit $899,195, no warning), '0x226' becomes 550, occupancy '0.85' is read as 0.85%.

Sample care time 20 min/horse/day (10.1 h/month) is half the Ohio State and a quarter of the UMD RES-10 per-horse labour figures; at 21 h/month the worked example loses $2,274.78 instead of showing $490.10 profit, so the example undercuts the tool's own 'your labour is not free' point. Uncited constant.

No depreciation / interest-on-investment line and one board tier only; extension enterprise budgets carry both and most barns sell pasture, stall and stall+paddock board at different prices and costs. Listed under 'Not decided' but not modelled.
Profit formula is written twice (profitAt and the inline profit in compute), a copy that can drift.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (verification 2; correctness 3, claims 3, median 3); finished (completeness 3). The arithmetic is right: profit, contribution margin, break-even occupancy, break-even and target board price and effective wage all match hand recomputation on two barns to the cent, and the method is the standard cost-volume-profit break-even. An equine extension business specialist would still not sign it off as an enterprise budget: the advice layer has a sign bug (an owner below break-even is told a couple of empty stalls would turn it into a loss), the effective hourly pay disappears exactly when the barn under-pays the owner, decimal-comma input inflates board a hundredfold silently, there is no depreciation, interest or board-tier mix, and the sample's 20 min/day care time is a quarter to a half of extension labour figures. Three of six seeded mutations in the findings logic left all 21 tests green.
